evidence.source: 漢字構形資料庫, Academia Sinica
evidence.text: The entry records a bronze example as 集成04315 and a Small Seal/說文 form. It interprets the form as 八 above 牛, with 八 indicating division and 牛 as the ox divided. This is the database’s analysis; the page does not display an oracle-bone form or independently establish a dated sequence.
evidence.title: 漢字「半」：字形演變

evidence.text: The entry quotes the received Shuowen definition ‘物中分也。从八，从牛。牛為物大，可以分也’ and gives Mandarin bàn. It documents senses for one half, a middle portion of time or space, very little, and partial/incomplete, with examples from Zhuangzi and later works. The entries do not establish when these senses arose or the links between them.
evidence.title: [A00435] 半 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（香港中文大學人文電算研究中心）
evidence.text: The entry assigns 八 both semantic and phonetic roles in its reported bronze analysis, proposes ‘split/open’ extending to ‘half,’ and attributes the proposal that 半 is an early graph of 判 to 何琳儀. It reports variants substituting 斗 or 升 for 牛 and 刃 for 斗, without establishing a complete dated order. It also reports 半 in a Mawangdui Zhouyi line where the received text has 磐桓. These remain source-reported analyses; the entry does not establish the sound of that manuscript token or the loan motivation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.text: The exact file page identifies this as an uploader-created, manually straightened vector depiction of a Shuowen Lesser Seal radical, uploaded 2013-12-09 by LiliCharlie and licensed CC BY-SA 3.0. This establishes the file’s stated provenance and reuse terms, but its pixels could not be inspected here; it is not evidence of an ancient artifact form.
evidence.title: File:Shuowen Seal Radical 018.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: Supplied local Baxter–Sagart table; 2014 dataset record
evidence.text: Supplied exact local rows in sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv give 八: Mandarin bā, Middle Chinese transcription peat, Old Chinese *pˤret; 半: Mandarin bàn, Middle Chinese transcription panH, Old Chinese *pˤan-s. Within Baxter–Sagart’s 2014 system the Old Chinese forms share an initial but have different endings. This is compatible with, but does not prove, the proposed phonetic role. The PDF was inaccessible in this invocation, so these readings are attributed to supplied local rows, not an opened PDF.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

evidence.source: Supplied local Unihan readings table; Unicode Consortium
evidence.text: Supplied local sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt rows give 八 bā, 半 bàn, and 牛 niú. These are current readings, not evidence for an ancient sound relation or pictorial analysis. The official per-character lookup pages were attempted but inaccessible, so the exact rows are not externally verified in this invocation.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup (八; also attempted U+534A 半 and U+725B 牛)

evidence.text: The official search page describes Unihan as a searchable character-property database and explains that Mandarin readings can be queried. This is current metadata, not historical pronunciation evidence.

gaps: No primary transcription or artifact image of the cited 集成04315 inscription was inspected; its specific reading and dating remain dependent on paleographic database records.
The inspected sources do not establish an oracle-bone form; nonappearance on these pages is not proof no such form exists.
The proposed semantic link ‘split/open’ to ‘half’ is undated. Later midpoint, incomplete/partial, and very-little senses are documented, but their chronology and paths are unresolved.
八’s proposed phonetic role is asserted by the CUHK database; the supplied Baxter–Sagart forms *pˤret and *pˤan-s have different endings, and this comparison does not establish the role.
The source publication and full argument attributed to 何琳儀 for 半 as an early graph of 判 were not inspected.

The CUHK report of 半 for 磐 in the Mawangdui Zhouyi was not checked against a primary manuscript facsimile or diplomatic transcription. No same-system comparison establishes the token’s Han-period sound basis; the spoken source word and the graph’s reading remain distinct questions.
No checked local Baxter–Sagart rows for 牛, 畔, or 磐 were needed for the adopted component account; no sound relation for them is asserted here.

Commons page content establishes stated file description and license, but the original SVG pixels could not be inspected, so the glyph’s visual identity and suitability for illustration remain unverified.
